text: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron:
Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When any man has a discharge from his body, the discharge makes him unclean.
This is his uncleanness from the discharge: whether his body runs with the discharge or is stopped up by it, he is unclean.

versions.text: This is how his uncleanness works with his discharge: whether his body lets the discharge flow freely or is blocked by it, he is unclean.
versions.explanation: "This is how his uncleanness works with his discharge" is vague and awkward for oral reading; the Hebrew simply states "this shall be his uncleanness in his discharge." The revised wording is tighter and closer to the Hebrew idiom of flowing versus being blocked.

text: Any bed the man with a discharge lies on becomes unclean, and anything he sits on becomes unclean.
Anyone who touches his bed must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Whoever sits on anything the man with a discharge has sat on must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Whoever touches the body of the man with a discharge must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
If the man with a discharge spits on someone who is clean, that person must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Every saddle the man with a discharge rides on becomes unclean.
Whoever touches anything that was under him will be unclean until evening, and whoever carries such things must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Anyone whom the man with a discharge touches without having rinsed his hands in water must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
A clay pot that the man with a discharge touches must be broken, and every wooden vessel must be rinsed with water.
When the man with a discharge is cleansed of it, he is to count off seven days for his cleansing, wash his clothes, and bathe his body in fresh running water; then he will be clean.
On the eighth day he must take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, come before the LORD at the entrance to the tent of meeting, and give them to the priest.
The priest is to offer them, one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. In this way the priest will make atonement for him before the LORD because of his discharge.
When a man has an emission of semen, he must bathe his whole body in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Any garment or leather that has semen on it must be washed with water, and it will be unclean until evening.
When a man lies with a woman and there is an emission of semen, both of them must bathe in water, and they will be unclean until evening.
When a woman has a discharge of blood from her body, she will be in her menstrual impurity for seven days, and anyone who touches her will be unclean until evening.
Anything she lies on during her period becomes unclean, and anything she sits on becomes unclean.
Anyone who touches her bed must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Anyone who touches anything she has sat on must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Whether it is the bed or anything she sits on, whoever touches it will be unclean until evening.
If a man lies with her and her impurity comes upon him, he will be unclean for seven days, and every bed he lies on becomes unclean.

When a woman has a discharge of blood for many days outside the time of her period, or when her discharge continues beyond her period, she will be unclean as long as the discharge lasts, just as during the days of her period.
Every bed she lies on while her discharge continues will be like the bed of her period, and anything she sits on will be unclean, as during her period.
Anyone who touches these things becomes unclean; he must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
When she is cleansed of her discharge, she is to count off seven days, and after that she will be clean.
On the eighth day she must take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them to the priest at the entrance to the tent of meeting.
The priest is to offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. In this way the priest will make atonement for her before the LORD because of her unclean discharge.
You must keep the Israelites separate from their uncleanness, so that they do not die in their uncleanness by defiling my dwelling place, which is among them.
This is the law for the man with a discharge, for anyone made unclean by an emission of semen,
for the woman in her menstrual impurity, for anyone with a discharge, male or female, and for the man who lies with a woman who is unclean.
